segments.en: The essential prayer is in the aspect of the evening Minchah offering — the aspect of the Prayer of the Poor — which is the aspect of hisbodidus and intimate conversation between oneself and one's Creator, the aspect of "before Hashem he pours out his speech." When one sees that the light is about to depart — which is the aspect of bein ha'arbayim [twilight] — one must then strengthen oneself in prayer and conversation, in the aspect of "Yitzchak went out to meditate in the field toward evening" [Bereishis 24:63], and pour out one's heart like water before Hashem before the day passes — in the aspect of "Woe unto us, for the day has turned, for the shadows of evening lengthen" [Yirmeyahu 6:4]. All the more so when a person sees that many of his days have already passed — and how much more so one whose days are mostly behind him and the day is beginning to grow dark. For man does not know his time, and our days are like a passing shadow. One must fulfill: "Remember your Creator… before the sun and the light grow dark" [Koheles 12:1–2]. And all this is the aspect of Tefillas HaMinchah, which is the aspect of teshuvah, as stated.

segments.he: וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת הַוִּדּוּי שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהַזְכִּיר הַחֲטָאִים וְהָעֲוֹנוֹת הַגְּמוּרִים בְּפֶה מָלֵא וּלְהַזְכִּיר בְּפֵרוּשׁ דְּבָרִים מְגֻנִּים כָּאֵלֶּה.
segments.en: The essential teshuvah is in the aspect of the Minchah prayer, which is the aspect of the Prayer of the Poor "ki ya'atof" [for he wraps himself in distress] — the aspect of the Minchah offering, which is the offering of the poor and destitute, being one-tenth of an ephah offered in the uttermost poverty. For the essential sacrifice now is prayer — which is the core of teshuvah: "Take with you words and return to Hashem" [Hoshaya 14:3]. As our Sages taught: "I ask of you nothing but words." And the primary worth of prayer and words before Hashem consists of the prayer and words of the poor and destitute.

segments.he: אֲבָל זֶהוּ כָּל תִּקּוּנוֹ. כִּי מֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּתְוַדֶּה וְאוֹמֵר חָטָאתִי הֲרֵי הוּא מוֹדֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא יָחִיד קַדְמוֹן נִמְצָא הַמְחֻיָּב יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ וּמוֹדֶה בְּתוֹרַת משֶׁה אֱמֶת שֶׁהַבּוֹרֵא הַיָּחִיד קַדְמוֹן הִזְהִירָנוּ עַל יְדֵי משֶׁה לִבְלִי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֵלּוּ הַחֲטָאִים רַק שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ הִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו וְכוּ' וּמוֹדֶה שֶׁחָטָא וְעִוֵּת בָּזֶה. כִּי בְּוַדַּאי הָיָה לוֹ כּחַ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגְדּוֹ וְכוּ', אַךְ אַף עַל פִּי כֵן מֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּתְוַדֶּה עַל הַחֲטָאִים וּמְבַקֵּשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה וּמְחִילָה, הֲרֵי הוּא מְחַפֵּשׂ וּמְבַקֵּשׁ עֲדַיִן אַיֵּה וְכוּ' כַּנַּ"ל וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר עֲלִיָּתוֹ כַּנַּ"ל:
segments.en: How exceedingly precious before Hashem is the prayer of the poor man who prays about his material needs and poverty — how much more so when a person feels his own poverty in deeds and his wretchedness before G-d. And when both kinds of poverty bear down upon him simultaneously — poverty of daas [mind-consciousness] from his many failings, and also material poverty so that his wife and children cry out for bread, clothing, and basic necessities — and yet he gathers himself and pours out his speech before Hashem from within his true poverty and distress, in the aspect of the Prayer of the Poor "ki ya'atof, v'lifnei Hashem yishpokh sicho" — this is exceedingly, exceedingly precious before Hashem. As it is written: "For He has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the poor man, nor has He hidden His face from him; and when he cried to Him, He listened" [Tehillim 22:25]. This implies that ordinarily it deserves to be despised, abhorred, and hidden from — yet His mercies are greatly abundant, and He does not despise it nor abhor it. As it is written: "I dwell with the contrite and lowly of spirit" [Yeshayahu 57:15], and: "You reduce a man to dust — to the very dust of crushing" [Tehillim 90:3, rendered according to Midrash].

segments.he: כּחַ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל גָּדוֹל מְאד וּבִפְרָט גּדֶל הַכּחַ שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיקִים הָעוֹסְקִים בְּתִקּוּנָם. עַל כֵּן אֲפִלּוּ אַחַר כָּל הַחֲטָאִים וְהָעֲוֹנוֹת הַגְּמוּרִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עֲדַיִן הַנְּשָׁמָה מַזְכֶּרֶת עַצְמָהּ בְּהָאֱמֶת וּמַרְגֶּשֶׁת כְּאֵבָהּ הֶעָצוּם שֶׁל עֲוֹנוֹתֶיהָ. עַד שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ עֲדַיִן תְּשׁוּבָה וּמְחִילָה וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ לוֹ תִּקְוָה יִהְיֶה אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה (הִלְכוֹת נְפִילַת אַפַּיִם הֲלָכָה ואות דה):
segments.en: See also in the Midrash Rabbah [on Vayikra, ch. 18] which greatly extols the Minchah offering and says as follows: "Not only that — all other offerings come whole, while this one comes half: half in the morning and half in the evening. Not only that — whoever brings it, the Torah accounts it as though he offered from one end of the world to the other, as it is said: 'From the rising of the sun until its setting…'" — see there. That is, the offering of the poor man, which is the core of teshuvah, pierces down to the depths and reaches from one end of the world to the other, to every person in the world, at every level, in every place — even to the most distant. For even the poorest and most minimal stirring, even the smallest good point, can bring one back to Hashem — only one must set aside one's arrogance, feel one's lowliness genuinely, and accustom oneself to pray and pour out one's speech before Him in the aspect of the Prayer of the Poor. One should pour out his speech like water — even if it seems to him that it is without wisdom or proper intention — yet nonetheless he should pour all that is in his heart before Him, in the aspect of "Pour out your heart like water before the face of Hashem" [Eichah 2:19]. This is extremely precious in Hashem's eyes, and through it one will merit to return and draw close to Him, in the aspect of "and to our G-d, for He multiplies forgiveness" [Yeshayahu 55:7].
